items.title: 52300_Trummy Young oral history interview
items.q: This guy was a fantastic trombone player in the '20's with Fletcher Henderson... Jimmy Harrison. He could play but he was drunk all the time, you know. And so, you'd go ask him something about a horn. Get away from here, kid, can't you see I'm busy.

ctx.x: I didn't -- I just played. I didn't know anything about taking care of the thing or anything. I just played it and that was it. When we came up we didn't -- you know, we didn't know anything about things like that. So, I teach kids today about horns. And the average kid playing the horn, they don't know really the proper care for a horn, how You should keep the horn clean and -- because I didn't know it. I try to help kids today.

And all the guys I knew, they were too busy to help us when I came long as kids. This guy was a fantastic trombone player in the '20's with Fletcher Henderson. And he played at Small's Paradise before -- Jimmy Harrison. He could play

but he was drunk all the time, you know. And so, you'd go ask him something about a horn. Get away from here, kid, can't you see I'm busy. He had chicks and all, but that's why I can never turn a kid down today because I think of those things. And actually, the guy probably know too much to tell me anyway because they really didn't know. You know, they hadn't made a scientific study of it. They really just didn't know. He couldn't have -- probably couldn't have told me.
